data.name: January
data.gender_notes: January is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: January is derived from the Latin word 'ianuarius', which is related to 'janua', meaning 'door'. January was named after the Roman god Janus, who is the god of beginnings, gates, doors, and endings. In many cultures, January represents a time of new beginnings and fresh starts. The name January carries the meaning “God's door” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose January usually hope their child will grow to embody god's door and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of new beginnings and the door to opportunities.
data.etymology: January belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's door.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of January total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.long_meaning: ינואר הוא השם העברי לחודש הראשון בשנה הגרגוריאנית, מקורו בשם הרומי יאנוארוס, שנתן השם לחודש הראשון בשנה, על שם האל הרומי יאנוס, אל הדלתות, ההתחלות והסופים, נוצרים רבים בוחרים לתת שם זה לילדיהם הנולדים בחודש ינואר, כהוקרה לשנה החדשה

in_greek.name: Ιανουάριος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Ιανουάριος είναι ο πρώτος μήνας του έτους στο Γρηγοριανό ημερολόγιο, πήρε το όνομά του από τον Ρωμαϊκό θεό Ιανό, που ήταν ο θεός των θυρών, των αρχών και των τελειών, οι Χριστιανοί συχνά επιλέγουν να ονομάσουν τα παιδιά τους Ιανουάριος, ως φόρο τιμής στον νέο χρόνο

in_latin.name: Ianuarius
in_latin.long_meaning: Ianuarius est nomen Latinum mensis primi anni, ab Ianuario, deo Romanorum ianuae, principiorum et finium, dictus, Christiani saepe hoc nomen infantibus suis qui mense Ianuario nati sunt, imponentes, ut novum annum honorerent

data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, January is a time to reflect on the previous year and look forward to the new one with hope and anticipation. It is also a time to remember the birth of Jesus, who is the door to salvation and the source of new life. (John 10:9)
